sections.html:
Cedar Falls is in Black Hawk County and forms the Waterloo-Cedar Falls metro area with Waterloo. The ZIP code is 50613 and the area code is 319. Population was 41,240 in mid-2025, compared with 40,713 at the 2020 count that ranked the city 13th in Iowa. The median age was 31.4, young for Iowa, which fits a city built around the University of Northern Iowa.

Cedar Falls is its own municipality with its own services, even though many buyers and employers treat it as one market with Waterloo next door. If you are moving within the metro, check which city's rules and school district apply to your next address. Older streets from the milling and railroad years sit beside postwar and newer areas, so houses of very different ages and conditions compete for the same buyers.

Most Cedar Falls addresses are in Cedar Falls Community Schools, which runs Cedar Falls High School, two junior high schools and seven elementary schools. One slice of Cedar Falls belongs to the Waterloo Community School District instead. Verify the district for your exact address before anyone writes it into an ad or an offer conversation. Private choices include Valley Lutheran High School and a Catholic elementary school at St. Patrick Catholic Church.

The city owns its power, gas, water and cable TV services, which run as Cedar Falls Utilities. That makes closing-day utility work simple, because one office handles most of it.

  • Call the utility early to schedule final meter readings for the closing date.
  • Ask for any unpaid balance in writing and settle it before the sale is final.
  • Mention the internet service when you describe the house. The utility began offering gigabit speeds on January 14, 2015, and PC Magazine named it the nation's fastest internet in 2020.

The Metropolitan Transit Authority of Black Hawk County runs public buses, which helps owners of houses near campus. Older neighbors may still mention the Malcolm Price Lab School, but it closed in 2012.

sections.h2: Iowa filings when a Cedar Falls house sells
sections.html:
Iowa adds a few filings to every sale. Each is set by statute and handled through the county recorder, so plan for them early.

Filing or chargeWhere it goesWhat it covers
Real estate transfer taxCounty recorder80 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. Nothing is owed when no consideration changes hands.
Declaration of valueRecorder, with the deedIowa Code 428A.2 names the transfers that are excused from filing it.
Groundwater hazard statementRecorder, with the deedWells, burial sites, underground tanks, hazardous waste, solid waste disposal sites and private sewage systems, under Iowa Code 558.69.

Nothing in the statute assigns the transfer tax to the buyer or the seller, so your purchase agreement should say who covers it. A deed that arrives at the recorder without a required statement gets turned away, which is why the title company checks the package before it is submitted. Filing the groundwater statement itself costs nothing.

The same three items show up whether the house sells for cash or through a listing. Ask the title company or attorney to confirm each is in the closing package a few days ahead, so a missing signature never pushes your closing date.

sections.h2: Black Hawk County property tax due dates
sections.html:
Iowa property tax is paid in two installments, and each turns delinquent on a fixed day. Delinquency starts October 1 for the first installment and April 1 for the second, as set out in Iowa Code 445.37.

Should September 30 or March 31 fall on a Saturday or Sunday, the cutoff slides to the second business day of the following month. A mailed payment with correct postage must be postmarked before the delinquent date to avoid interest.

A mid-year sale usually means the buyer and seller divide the tax bill at the closing date. The county treasurer can tell you what is already paid, so the settlement numbers line up. Keep the receipts with your sale papers.

sections.h2: What slows down Cedar Falls sales
sections.html:
Most delays come from paperwork about the property itself, plus whatever work an older house needs. These are the usual causes:

  • A private well, septic system or buried tank that has to be disclosed on the groundwater hazard statement.
  • Deferred repairs that make a traditional buyer's inspection list long.
  • A tenant in place, or a lease that ends at a bad time.
  • An inherited home where the title is not yet in the heirs' names.

Each one can slow a conventional sale. Selling to a cash buyer removes the loan appraisal step, though the recorder filings above still apply.

Tenants deserve a plain plan. If someone lives in the house, decide whether the buyer takes it with the lease in place or whether the unit will be empty by closing, and put that in writing before you accept an offer. For an inherited house, sort out who holds title first. A buyer, a title company and the recorder all need the names on the deed to match the people signing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Cedar Falls house work?
sections.html:
Recording works the same way for a cash sale as for any other, but fewer things happen before closing. You tell the buyer about the house, the buyer looks it over, and the offer reflects the house in its current shape. Nobody has to wait on a mortgage approval or tidy up for showings.

  1. Share the address and the condition of the house, along with any tenant or title issues.
  2. Review the written offer and ask any question about it.
  3. Once you say yes, a title company or attorney drafts the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement.
  4. Sign, record at the Black Hawk County Recorder, and receive the proceeds.

Turning an offer down costs you nothing. Weigh it against the expense and the months a listing would take. Listing means preparing the house, allowing showings and waiting through a buyer's inspection and appraisal, while a cash offer is priced on the condition you describe.

Closing day itself is short. Your part is to sign the deed and the filings, hand over the keys and confirm where the proceeds should go. The title company records the deed and pays off any balance still owed on the house from the sale money.

A short folder of papers speeds up any Cedar Falls closing, cash or not.

  • The deed and anything you have on how title is held, plus court or heir paperwork if the house was inherited.
  • Notes on any well, burial site, underground tank, waste site or private sewage system, so the groundwater statement is accurate. If none exist, the deed carries a short statement saying so.
  • Paid property tax receipts from the Black Hawk County treasurer.
  • Lease copies and a move-out plan if anyone rents the house.
  • A recent utility statement from Cedar Falls Utilities, so the final reading and balance are easy to line up.

The seller or the seller's agent signs the groundwater statement, so answer each item from what you actually know about the lot.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cedar Falls, Iowa?
faqs.a: About 41,240 people lived in Cedar Falls in mid-2025. The 2020 count was 40,713, which ranked the city 13th among Iowa cities.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies when I sell a house in Cedar Falls?
faqs.a: The rate in Iowa Code 428A.1 is 80 cents per $500 of value, rounding any leftover amount up to the next $500. If the transfer has no consideration, there is no tax. The sales contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose a well or septic system when selling in Cedar Falls?
faqs.a: Yes, if the property has one. Iowa Code 558.69 requires a groundwater hazard statement that reports wells, private sewage systems, underground tanks, burial sites and certain waste conditions. If none exist, the deed carries a short statement saying so.

faqs.q: When is the second property tax installment delinquent in Iowa?
faqs.a: It becomes delinquent on April 1. When March 31 is a weekend day, the clock starts on the second business day in April.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale skip the recorder filings?
faqs.a: No. The deed, declaration of value and groundwater statement are still recorded in Black Hawk County. What a cash sale skips is the lender's appraisal and loan approval.
